adversarial_notes: U1-U3, U5: a validator can pass vacuously (grep pipelines hide the exit status). Mitigation: exit status taken from the process itself and printed as EXIT:; the gate additionally enforces G1-G5 (PASS-line count equals SUMMARY, no FAIL line, no baseline check dropped). U1-U3 were run one at a time; tools/ is unchanged vs HEAD afterwards.

U4: closeout passes at V=1.4.0 by comparing anchors to one another; it would pass vacuously if every anchor were stale together. Cross-checked: ROADMAP line 825 and the git tag v1.4.0 (annotated, peeled 9edd5d0) agree.
U6: schema validity is vacuous if the schema has no required keys. Each schema has required keys (4, 4, 4, 8) and dropping the first required key was rejected (negative control).

U7: 'identical to HEAD' is vacuous if both sides are empty or compared by length. Compared 231 entries deeply and under canonical serialization; a perturbed copy is detected; HEAD scope_budget is non-empty and differs from the new one.

U8: lifecycle fields can agree while the dependency graph is wrong. Also checked: all dependency ids resolve, no other phase is in_progress, 099 is in the computed eligible set, feature_list phase equals run_state current_phase.

U9: the committed *.txt captures could be stale. Tools were re-executed in this context and diffed. 9a and 9d are byte-identical. 9b and 9c diverge only through V11, whose package-confinement set does not list .agent/validator/phase-014-activation.json (created after the captures). Isolation proof: on a copy of the repo without that file, 9b PASSes (only the V11 path count differs, 38 vs 58, the Evaluator's own eval/ files) and 9c is 10/10 and identical to the capture. The negative-control tool also guards against vacuity: it requires the unmutated copy to pass AND every mutation to fail, so a V11 false positive is exactly what it reports as BAD.

U10: re-hashing from a table the checker itself extracts could be circular. The table is extracted from the feature list, the file set on disk is enumerated independently (7 = 7, none unpinned), the AT7 command is run verbatim, and a zeroed pin makes it fail.

U11: reading the function alone does not show peeling; shown empirically that it passes through whatever is recorded, and that the peel is bootstrap.sh:464. The claim as worded holds only transitively; the evidence says so rather than overclaiming.

U12/U13: 'acknowledged.' is a very short quote; finding it verbatim somewhere is weak evidence on its own. It is anchored by its run_state timestamp, and the check also scans for near-miss paraphrases of each quote stem, finding none. The CHANGELOG regex check has a planted-token control.

U14: the Evaluator's own eval/ directory sits under .agent/evidence/phase-014-activation/, the directory the spec calls frozen. AT7 pins only the 7 listed files, so the pins are unaffected, and the eval/ files are inside the allowed .agent/ scope. Note the 7 files on disk outside eval/ were counted for unit 10 with eval/ excluded.
U15: the check inspects only *.txt; .json/.md evidence is out of its scope. The in-flight capture of unit14_15 cannot check itself; verified by head/tail after the run.

Extra: gh run view --json jobs does expose databaseId (run 37769000595: validate/e2e_bootstrap/fixtures_self_test, all success; unit16_gh_jobs_databaseid.txt), the item the validator listed as owed. Unit 11 and unit 09e created a few small mktemp directories under /tmp (pin-sem-*), outside the repo; removal was blocked by the permission system, harmless. Coverage warning not applicable (docs/planning change). Circuit breaker: first evaluation of this review, no strike history.

Rev 2, V11: the allowlist is an exact-equality tuple, so a look-alike or a sibling verdict file cannot ride it. The 4 new controls use the REAL git status text plus injected lines, so they cannot pass on an empty status; the unmutated control uses no flag at all and so exercises the real git status call. A V11 weakness that predates this fix and is not part of it: PACKAGE_PATHS entries without a trailing slash (docs/planning/backlog_dag.json, CHANGELOG.md, docs/planning/ROADMAP.md and so on) are matched with startswith, so a look-alike such as CHANGELOG.md.bak would be admitted (read from source line 317, not exercised). Not blocking, since such paths remain inside unit 14's scope guard, but worth hardening to exact-or-directory matching.

Rev 2: my unit 9f grep for non-membership uses of ORCHESTRATOR_OWNED matched line 317 only because that line also calls startswith on PACKAGE_PATHS, a different tuple; no prefix test applies to ORCHESTRATOR_OWNED.
Rev 2: the recaptured .txt files differ from my reruns only in V11 path counts, which grow with my own eval/ evidence files.
